title: Khalji Dynasty
capsule: The Khalji dynasty was the second ruling house of the Delhi Sultanate, founded by Jalal ud-Din Firuz Khalji in 1290 after the overthrow of the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty. Its most consequential ruler, Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296–1316), conquered Gujarat (1297), Rajputana, and led the first Muslim armies deep into the Deccan under generals Malik Kafur, extracting vast tribute and briefly bringing Madurai under nominal Delhi suzerainty by 1311 — the widest territorial reach the sultanate ever achieved. Alauddin also implemented radical market-control reforms in Delhi, fixing commodity prices and maintaining a standing professional army. The dynasty collapsed rapidly after his death: a series of short-lived sultans succumbed to factional violence before the throne was seized by the usurper Khusrau Khan, whom Ghiyasuddin Tughluq overthrew in 1320, founding the Tughluq dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial extent derived from chronicle accounts of Khalji military campaigns and tax-collection records; the Deccan frontier is approximate, as tributaries were not administratively incorporated, and the polygon boundary reflects the outer range of tribute extraction rather than administered territory.
